problem.title: Does this sound familiar?

cards.title: Referrals as the only channel
cards.text: New projects come almost exclusively through referrals and existing contacts. That works as long as your network delivers. When it does is not up to you.

cards.title: Acquisition happens on the side
cards.text: Leadership handles sales personally, whenever there's time. As soon as a project is on fire, new business grinds to a halt.

cards.title: A project ending means uncertainty
cards.text: A major project is wrapping up and there's no follow-up in sight. So you start calling around your network, under time pressure.

problem.consequence: The consequences: consultants without a project, revenue you never get back, and growth plans on hold.
problem.bridge: Where do you stand right now? Find out in 3 minutes.

about.title: Who's behind NGCX
paragraphs: I'm Kewin, founder of NGCX. [PLACEHOLDER: two or three sentences on your professional background and why you specialize in IT consultancies and software agencies.]
With NGCX, I want to give IT consultancies and software agencies something many of them lack: new business that doesn't depend on chance, but on a process you can measure and improve.
about.pilot: NGCX is in its early stages. We are deliberately starting with a small number of pilot partners to prove together what works. We'll show references as soon as we have real ones.

items.a: NGCX supports you in B2B client acquisition: from defining your target clients and researching relevant companies and decision-makers to targeted outreach, pipeline management and regular reporting.
For IT consultancies and software agencies in the DACH region with around 10 to 50 employees that want to make their client acquisition more predictable. NGCX focuses exclusively on this market.

items.q: What does working with NGCX cost?
items.a: Our pricing is transparent: Pipeline Core and Pipeline Growth each consist of a one-time setup and monthly support. You'll find all amounts and terms on our pricing page. We'll work out which plan fits in a free initial call.
No. Whether a deal comes about depends on many factors outside our control. We agree on measurable targets for our work up front and make progress transparent.

We start by analyzing your current situation together and defining your target clients. Building on that, we develop the messaging and process, put them into practice and report to you regularly on progress.

items.q: How much effort does it take on our side?
items.a: Very little. After a short alignment call, we take over research, outreach and pipeline management entirely. Your time goes where it counts: conversations with interested companies.

items.q: How is this different from hiring a salesperson?
items.a: A permanent hire means recruiting, onboarding and long-term costs. NGCX gives you a structured sales process without having to build these structures in-house.

items.q: Does this make sense if we already grow through referrals?
items.a: Yes. Referrals remain a valuable channel, but they are hard to steer. Structured client acquisition complements them and makes your order book less dependent on chance.

levels.title: Referral-dependent
levels.text: Your growth is in other people's hands. That works until it suddenly doesn't.

levels.title: Pipeline by chance
levels.text: There's a foundation, but new clients don't come in predictably yet. Usually it's the one building block that connects everything that's missing.

levels.title: Predictable sales
levels.text: You're further along than most consultancies your size. Now it's about scaling deliberately.

areas.name: Target client clarity
areas.weak: Without a clearly defined ideal client, acquisition becomes a shot in the dark: you reach out to many and hardly reach the right ones.
areas.mid: You roughly know who you want. What's missing is precision: concrete triggers and names instead of just industries.
areas.strong: You know exactly who you want. That's the foundation most firms lack.
areas.teaser: NGCX turns this into a target list of real decision-makers who may have a need right now.

areas.name: Acquisition engine
areas.weak: Your growth depends on referrals and on the managing director's time. If both dry up, things get tight.
areas.mid: Acquisition happens, but not reliably. As soon as day-to-day business heats up, sales grinds to a halt.
areas.strong: New clients don't just come to you by chance. Now it's about scaling that.
areas.teaser: NGCX builds an acquisition process that keeps running, even while you're deep in a project.

areas.name: Outreach & messaging
areas.weak: If a decision-maker doesn't immediately understand which problem you solve, your message is gone within three seconds.
areas.mid: Your message is there, but not yet tailored to the recipient's role and situation.
areas.strong: Your message lands. Now it's about consistently getting it in front of the right people.
areas.teaser: NGCX develops outreach that decision-makers actually read.

areas.name: Pipeline & steering
areas.weak: Without an overview of your pipeline, you only notice bottlenecks once the project has already ended.
areas.mid: You have data, but don't yet use it to course-correct in time.
areas.strong: You steer your sales with numbers. Few consultancies your size do that.
areas.teaser: NGCX shows how many conversations you need to reach your goals and where things get stuck.

questions.t: How would you describe your ideal new client?
o: “Basically any company that needs IT.”
Industry and size are roughly clear.
Industry, size, typical triggers and decision-makers are defined in writing.

questions.t: Do you know which events trigger demand for your services?
o: Not really, inquiries just come in.
We have an idea, but don't actively monitor it.
Yes, we know the triggers and watch for them deliberately.

questions.t: Do you know the specific decision-makers at your target companies?
o: No, we only know the company names.
For a few companies, yes.
Yes, we keep an up-to-date list with names and roles.

questions.t: Where did your last 5 new clients come from?
o: All through referrals or existing contacts.
Mostly referrals, 1–2 from our own outreach.
The majority from active outreach of our own.

questions.t: Who takes care of new client acquisition?
o: Leadership, when there's time left over.
Leadership, in fixed time blocks.
A set process or person, independent of day-to-day business.

questions.t: A major project ends in 6 weeks. What happens?
o: Mild panic, we start calling around our network.
There are a few conversations, but nothing certain.
The follow-up is usually already in the pipeline.

questions.t: Why should a decision-maker hire you specifically? What would they say?
o: “Good people, fair price.”
Your specialization is roughly recognizable.
They can clearly say which problem you solve and with what result.

questions.t: How is your first message to a new contact created?
o: Written spontaneously, from scratch every time.
One template that's the same for everyone.
Tailored to role and situation, tested and improved.

questions.t: A contact doesn't respond to the first message. What then?
o: Then we leave it.
Sometimes yes, sometimes no, depending on time.
There's a fixed sequence of further touchpoints.

questions.t: Where are your open sales opportunities documented?
o: In our heads or our inboxes.
In Excel or a CRM, but updated irregularly.
In an up-to-date CRM with clear stages.

questions.t: Do you know how many first meetings you need per month to hit your revenue targets?
o: No idea.
Roughly, based on gut feeling.
Yes, based on our closing rates.

questions.t: How often do you look at your sales numbers?
o: Only when there are problems.
About once a quarter.
Monthly or more often, with fixed reporting.
